title: Contact Finishing
description: A two-player drill with a pad or bump at the rim that trains finishing through contact, and-one toughness, and free-throw conversion.
goal: Build the strength and body control to finish at the rim through real defensive contact and convert and-one opportunities.
setup: One player is the finisher, the other is the defender with a blocking pad — or uses a controlled body bump if no pad is available.
Finisher starts at the wing or top with the ball; defender waits near the paint.
Rotate roles every 5 makes so both players get contact reps.

instructions.title: Drive and absorb contact
instructions.detail: Finisher attacks the rim at speed while the defender bumps with the pad at the gather — finisher must keep the ball high and finish.

instructions.title: Two-foot power finishes
instructions.detail: Gather into a two-foot jump stop and go up strong through the bump, using the rim to protect the ball from the defender.

instructions.title: And-one free throws
instructions.detail: After every make through contact, the finisher immediately shoots one free throw — makes the and-one habit automatic.

instructions.title: Switch sides and roles
instructions.detail: Do 5 makes driving right and 5 driving left, then swap roles and repeat.

coachingPoints: Initiate the contact yourself — a finisher who seeks the bump stays balanced; one who avoids it gets knocked off line.
Keep the ball high and tight on the gather — low balls get stripped on contact.
Go up strong with two hands on the gather, then finish with one — never bring the ball down to your waist.
Land balanced and be ready for the putback; contact finishes often need a second effort.
commonMistakes: Fading away from contact — drifting sideways turns an and-one into a blocked shot.
Bringing the ball down on the bump — keep it chin-to-rim high through the hit.
progression: Defender contests vertically with a hand up instead of just bumping, finisher must score through two consecutive bumps, or add a help defender rotating over.
regression: Use lighter bumps, start the drive closer to the rim, or remove the defender and focus on two-foot power mechanics first.
gameApplication: Playoff and late-game basketball is physical — players who finish through contact draw fouls and convert three-point plays instead of settling.
